On one night every year, millions of people refuse to look at the moon. Stay till the end, because even Krishna was cursed by it.

As the story goes, Ganesha once tripped after a big feast, and the moon laughed at him. So Ganesha cursed it. Whoever looks at you on my day will be falsely accused. Years later, on that very night, Krishna saw the moon, just its reflection in a cup of milk.

But soon, a priceless jewel called Syamantaka went missing, and all of Dwarka whispered, Krishna stole it. Krishna didn't argue. He went into the forest alone, followed the trail to a dark cave, and fought a mighty bear for twenty-eight days.
Wait, who was the bear? Jambavan, the old hero from Lord Ram's army. When he finally recognised Krishna, he fell at His feet, and gave back the jewel.
That's why on Ganesh Chaturthi, we don't look at the moon. And if we do, we hear this story to clear our name. Comment Ganesha, and send this to someone who was blamed for something they didn't do.
